knowledge.title: Patient AI Actions panel (right side)
knowledge.content:
On the right of an open patient: "AI Patient Summary" and "AI Result Summary" (the app's AI wrote them — say so when you quote them), then "Patient AI Actions (covers N unfiled results)" with a count; "Open AI actions" (✦, bottom right) opens it when it is closed.
- Each suggestion is a card: its kind (ADD TASK, ADD DIAGNOSIS, ADD RECALL, DRAFT EMAIL, DRAFT TEXT), a text box with the AI's words (Task subject, Diagnosis name, Add Recall, Draft Email, Draft Text), "Dismiss suggestion", and its button: Add task (and Add urgent), Add diagnosis, Add recall, Send email, Send Text.
- "Add task" opens "QUICK EDIT" in the card (priority Normal); "Add urgent" does the same with priority Urgent — use it only when the user said urgent. QUICK EDIT: TASK, DUE DATE (DD/MM/YYYY), PRIORITY (Normal, Medium, Urgent), ASSIGN TO, LOCATION; then Dismiss, Cancel, "Full Form" (the full Add Task form, filled from it) and "Create" (saves it).
- Which card: the one whose text matches what the user asked for; several alike — ask. Change the card's text only to the user's words. Each Add, Create, Dismiss, Send — the user approves it. Send email / Send Text go to the patient: only when the user asked, to the address the user gave.
- An added or dismissed suggestion leaves the list (the count goes down). Check the result: a task, recall or diagnosis then shows in Indici (the patient's Task list, Recalls, Diagnosis).

knowledge.title: Add a task (AI card, Full Form or Actions menu)
knowledge.trigger: add the suggested task for aqib, due next week
knowledge.content:
Which way: the user names an AI suggestion ("the suggested task", "the AI recall", its words) → its card in Patient AI Actions (rule "Patient AI Actions panel"); the user says "full form" → the card's Full Form; otherwise the quick edit. A new one the AI didn't suggest → the Actions menu (task, recall) — never change a suggestion's card into something else.
Fill only what the user gave; leave the AI's filled values unless the user changed them; ask for a required field still empty. Each Add, Create and Save — the user approves it. After saving, check it on the page (the card left the list, or the form closed with no error) before saying it was added; if you can't see it, say so.
1. AI card ADD TASK: "Add task" (or "Add urgent" only when the user said urgent) opens QUICK EDIT — TASK (the subject), DUE DATE (DD/MM/YYYY), PRIORITY (Normal, Medium, Urgent), ASSIGN TO, LOCATION. Change what the user gave, then "Create".
2. Full Form (from the quick edit): "Add Task — Full form, AI PRE-FILLED": Location, To*, From, Priority*, Start*, Due In, Due*, Start Time, End Time, Type, Subject / Progress* (its box is named "Write Recall Notes"); "Save task".
3. A new task: open_menu ["Actions", "Create Task"] — the same form, empty, comes with the result (no wait or read needed). Type the subject into "Write Recall Notes" (Subject / Progress*); Start and Due are today unless the user gave a date; then "Save task". Several tasks: one after another the same way, each its own Save.

knowledge.title: Add a recall (AI card, Full Form or Actions menu)
knowledge.trigger: add the AI recall for aqib with the full form
knowledge.content:
Which way: the user names an AI suggestion ("the suggested task", "the AI recall", its words) → its card in Patient AI Actions (rule "Patient AI Actions panel"); the user says "full form" → the card's Full Form; otherwise the quick edit. A new one the AI didn't suggest → the Actions menu (task, recall) — never change a suggestion's card into something else.
Fill only what the user gave; leave the AI's filled values unless the user changed them; ask for a required field still empty. Each Add, Create and Save — the user approves it. After saving, check it on the page (the card left the list, or the form closed with no error) before saying it was added; if you can't see it, say so.
1. AI card ADD RECALL: "Add recall" opens QUICK EDIT — RECALL GROUP (select_option) and RECALL DATE (filled); then "Create".
2. Full Form (from the quick edit): "Add Recall — Full form, AI PRE-FILLED": Provider*, Recall Group*, Description* (its list follows the group), Notes (the AI's words, filled), Priority (Medium), Recall In* (sets the Due Date), Due Date*, Actual Recall Date, Cycle (Yearly), tick boxes Active, Confidential, Do not show on Portal; "Save".
3. A new recall: Actions › Create Recall — the same form, empty; "Save".
Recall Group and Description: ask the user when they didn't say, listing what the dropdown shows (e.g. Bloods → CBC, HBA1C…).

knowledge.title: Add a diagnosis (AI card or its Full Form)
knowledge.trigger: add the suggested diagnosis dyslipidaemia for aqib
knowledge.content:
Which way: the user names an AI suggestion ("the suggested task", "the AI recall", its words) → its card in Patient AI Actions (rule "Patient AI Actions panel"); the user says "full form" → the card's Full Form; otherwise the quick edit. A new one the AI didn't suggest → Actions (task, recall) — never change a suggestion's card into something else.
Fill only what the user gave; leave the AI's filled values unless the user changed them; ask for a required field still empty. Each Add, Create and Save — the user approves it. After saving, check it on the page (the card left the list, or the form closed with no error) before saying it was added; if you can't see it, say so.
A diagnosis is added only from an AI card here — Actions has none; for one the AI didn't suggest, tell the user it is added in Indici's consult.
1. AI card ADD DIAGNOSIS: "Add diagnosis" opens QUICK EDIT — DIAGNOSIS NAME, DETAILS (the AI's summary), DIAGNOSIS TYPE (e.g. disorder, finding); then "Create".
2. Full Form (from the quick edit): "Add Diagnosis — Full form, AI PRE-FILLED": Concept ID, Synonym, Fully Specified Name; Diagnosis Options (tick boxes) Long Term, Problem List, Highlight, Add Recall, Confidential, Do not show on Portal, Add To CarePlan; Diagnosis Status Confirmed / Interim / Suspected / Probable; Onset Date; Notes; "Save" ("Health Pathways" and "Up-to Date" only show information).
Tick an option or choose a status only when the user said it.
- A save that answers "Something went wrong, Please try again" did not save. The Full Form does this when its Concept ID is <UNKNOWN> (the AI found no code for the diagnosis): tell the user, and offer the quick edit's Create instead — don't press Save again. The quick edit's Create can answer the same: then this diagnosis can't be saved here either way — don't offer the Full Form; tell the user it is added in Indici's consult ("Go to Consult for <name>", only when the user says yes).

knowledge.title: Medications in the Smart AI Inbox
knowledge.content: The Smart AI Inbox can't add, change or stop a medication — it only shows them (Clinical Summary › Medications). Asked to add one: tell the user it is done in Indici's consult, and offer to open it with "Go to Consult for <name>" (it opens in Indici, where Indici's workflow "Add a medication in the consult" applies). Open it only when the user says yes.

knowledge.title: Dropdowns and pop-up forms (Smart AI Inbox)
knowledge.content:
- Every dropdown here (Provider, Recall Group, Description, Recall In, Priority, Cycle, To, Location, Type, the search filters) is a custom one: choose with select_option and the option's text, e.g. select_option(Recall Group, "Bloods") — don't type into it or click its options yourself. A dropdown whose list follows another (Description after Recall Group) is chosen after that one. If select_option says there is no such option, it lists the ones there: ask the user which.
- Never press Escape in a pop-up form: it closes the form and loses what was filled. Leave a form only with its Cancel or Close, and only when the user wants it left.
- Stay on the way the user asked for (the AI card, its Full Form, or the Actions menu); if it doesn't work, tell the user instead of starting the same thing another way.

knowledge.title: Trend of a patient's results (CBC and other tests)
knowledge.trigger: show me the trend for this patient's cbc
knowledge.content:
"This patient" is the one open on the right. The user named a patient who isn't open: open them first (workflow "Open a patient and a record"). No name and none open: ask which.
1. Show the patient's earlier records too, in one step: open_menu ["Inbox scope for <name>", "Show all for this patient"]. The records list under the name, and the page comes with the result.
2. Read them in one step with read_records: area "Go to Consult" (a record shows in the page, not a pop-up: always give it), next "Next", status_label "Status", normal_values "Normal", empty_is_normal true, max 100; first empty when the record showing is "1 / n", otherwise first = the patient's first record button in the list ("<subject> <date>"). Use only that patient's records, and only those of the kind asked (CBC: the records whose subject or tests are a blood count — haemoglobin, WBC, platelets, ferritin…).
3. Answer with a table: one row per test, one column per result date, oldest first, the values as the records show them; a last column with the direction (↑ rising, ↓ falling, → steady) from the first to the last value. Mark each value outside its reference range (or flagged High/Low).
4. Then "Summary": 2–3 sentences, not a list: which values changed, in which direction, and which are now outside the range. Dates are DD/MM/YYYY; say how long they span by working it out from the first and last date. Say a record is flagged only for those whose own status or red text marks it, by date — not "the records" as a whole. Only what the records show — no diagnosis of your own; say it is for the clinician to review.
Then offer the actions it calls for, numbered, one line each (Task, Diagnosis, Medication — a medication is added in Indici), and ask which to add; do none yet.

knowledge.title: Issues in a report — mammogram, discharge summary or any record
knowledge.trigger: show me issues in this mammogram; what are the issues in this discharge summary
knowledge.content:
"This" record is the one open on the right (its page comes with the request — no extra reads). A record showing only "No document attachment" can't be read: say so. Answer from the report's words only.
1. Key findings: the abnormal ones first, each with the report's words or value and its flag.
2. Issues: what needs action and why — an abnormal finding or result with no plan, a recommended follow-up (biopsy, referral, repeat test or X-ray) not arranged, a result still out of range, medicines (dose, how long), allergies missing or conflicting, anything left unclear.
   Mammogram: the BI-RADS category and what it asks for (0 more imaging; 1–2 routine screening; 3 short-interval follow-up; 4–5 biopsy; 6 known cancer), the side and size, lymph nodes, and the recommendation.
   Discharge summary: the diagnosis, treatment, discharge medicines, results at discharge, follow-up asked of the GP, and what was not arranged.
3. "Summary": 2–3 sentences, not a list.
Then offer the actions it calls for, numbered, one line each (Task, Diagnosis, Medication — a medication is added in Indici), and ask which to add; do none yet.

knowledge.title: Why a record is abnormal
knowledge.trigger: why is this record abnormal
knowledge.content:
The record open on the right. Decide abnormal as the rule "Normal and abnormal (Smart AI Inbox)" says — the STATUS flags, or the list's red colour.
1. Name each flagged test: its value, its reference range and which side it is on (high or low), or the report's words for a finding (e.g. "BI-RADS 4C — suspicious").
2. Say in plain words what each means, without a diagnosis of your own.
3. No flag but shown red: say the app marks it abnormal, and which values are outside their range. Nothing flagged and not red: it is normal — say so.
4. "Summary": 2–3 sentences, not a list.

knowledge.title: Suggested actions for a record — review, save or dismiss
knowledge.trigger: add a task against this record; add diagnosis against this record; add medication against this record; save selected actions and dismiss the remaining ones
knowledge.content:
After an analysis (a trend, issues, why abnormal) with no action asked for, offer the actions it calls for, numbered, each one line — e.g. "1. Task: Follow up BI-RADS 4C mammogram — book biopsy (Urgent)", "2. Diagnosis: …", "3. Medication: … (added in Indici)". Do none of them until the user picks.
The app's own AI suggestions are the cards in "Patient AI Actions" on the right: each its kind (ADD TASK, ADD DIAGNOSIS, ADD RECALL…), its text, its Add button and "Dismiss suggestion". The ✦ button "Open AI actions; no pending actions", or "No pending AI actions" in the panel, means there are none — don't open it. Cards showing: list them too, numbered.
"Add a task / diagnosis / medication against this record" is the user's pick already: do it now, on the record open on the right — no list of options, no asking which, and no asking for a date or priority (today and the form's default). The approval card before the save is the user's check. Its words come from the record (subject and the issue, e.g. "Follow up: [record subject] — haemoglobin falling"), unless the user gave them.
- Task: an AI card ADD TASK that matches → its Add button and Create (Full Form when the user says so); none → open_menu ["Actions", "Create Task"] (workflow "Add a task").
- Diagnosis: an AI card ADD DIAGNOSIS that matches → workflow "Add a diagnosis"; none → it is added in Indici's consult: ask only for a yes, and for the diagnosis if neither the user nor the record names one — never make one up.
- Medication: rule "Medications in the Smart AI Inbox" — Indici's consult.
"Save selected actions and dismiss the remaining ones": selected = the ones the user named (numbers or words) in the list you gave or the AI cards. No list yet, or nothing named — show the list and ask which. Then: each selected → its Add button and Create (Full Form when the user said "full form"), or for one from your own list: a task → open_menu ["Actions", "Create Task"], type the subject into "Write Recall Notes", "Save task"; another kind → its workflow; each other AI card → "Dismiss suggestion". The rest of your own list is only text — nothing in the app to dismiss: leave them and say they were not added. Never scroll or search for AI cards the page doesn't show. The user approves each one. Check the count went down; then answer what was saved and what was dismissed.
Save option: the quick edit's Create unless the user named one ("full form", "urgent"). After the actions, a comment on the record or filing it — only when the user asks.

knowledge.title: Attention Providers — send a record to a provider
knowledge.content:
"Attention Providers" (on the open record, beside the Diagnostic Comment) opens the pop-up "Attention Providers": "Assigning this record only.", "Selected: <provider>" (who has it now), the box "Search provider by name", one choice per provider ("<initials> <name> Provider"), Cancel and Assign.
- To send the record to a provider (or "assign it to <name>"): type the name into "Search provider by name", click that provider's choice, then Assign — the user approves Assign. Several providers match: list them and ask which.
- "Who is this record assigned to?": open it and read "Selected:", then Cancel — nothing changes.
- It assigns the open record only; for several records, do it record by record.

knowledge.title: Practice, location, sign-in and what the screen shows
knowledge.content:
- The practice button at the top ("Victoria Clinic") opens the practices: "Currently Selected" marks the one in use. The location button beside it ("Victoria Clinic 1") opens the locations the same way. Choosing another changes whose inbox shows: only when the user asks for that practice or location by name — use the names the menu shows, never assume one.
- The user's button ("<name> <practice> - <location>") opens System Settings and Sign Out. Sign Out ends the sign-in: only when the user asks; the user approves.
- "Toggle patient list" hides or shows the patient list on the left; "Collapse search controls" / "Expand search controls" hide or show the search bar; "Pin search controls" keeps the bar open after a search. They change only the view.
- A patient's "Collapse test records" / "Expand test records" hides or shows its records under its name in the list.
- "Refresh inbox" loads new records now (it refreshes every 60 s on its own).

knowledge.title: Pin a patient (keep at the top)
knowledge.content: "Pin patient" beside a patient's name marks the patient as critical: the patient stays at the top of the list. It saves at once (for every user of the inbox); "Unpin patient" undoes it. Click it only when the user asks to pin or unpin that patient — the user approves. "Which patients are pinned?": the ones whose button says "Unpin patient".

knowledge.title: The document of a record (viewer)
knowledge.content:
A record with a document (a referral, discharge summary, scanned letter) shows it under "Document — Original report", with its own bar: the zoom ("80%", "Zoom in", "Zoom out"), "Toggle page view mode" (All pages, or Single page with "n / m"), "Toggle fullscreen" and "Open in new tab". They change only the view; read the document's text from the page (read_page content) — zooming or opening it in a new tab is only when the user asks for it.
- Only a record with a document has this bar. The open record has none ("No document attachment", or its text and results show without a document): say so in one line — never open other records to find one with a document, unless the user names that record.
- The patient's email address and phone at the top are buttons: the email opens "Send Email" for that address, the phone opens Call and Send Text (workflow "Actions menu").
